questions.stem: This H&E-stained histologic field appears in a discussion of conditions that cause anemia of chronic disease. The dense basophilic (blue-purple) cellularity shown is most characteristic of which tissue process?

explanation.summary: The field is packed with small, densely staining mononuclear cells typical of a chronic inflammatory (lymphocyte/plasma-cell) infiltrate. Sustained inflammation of this kind drives the cytokine response (IL-6) that underlies anemia of chronic disease, rather than the fat, neutrophilic pus, dense collagen, or striated fibers of the other choices.

questions.stem: This signaling schematic shows the central hormone of iron regulation that is upregulated in chronic inflammation, leading to internalization and degradation of ferroportin-1. Which inflammatory mediator most directly drives increased production of this hormone?

explanation.summary: IL-6 is the principal inflammatory cytokine that stimulates hepatic synthesis of hepcidin. Elevated hepcidin causes internalization and degradation of ferroportin-1, blocking iron release from enterocytes, macrophages, and hepatocytes, so less iron reaches the marrow and anemia results. IL-10 and TGF-beta are anti-inflammatory, IFN-gamma is not the primary hepcidin driver, and erythropoietin actually suppresses hepcidin.
